audience.programmeDescription: Medicine at Erasmus University Rotterdam combines biomedical science with clinical reasoning, patient-centred skills, research and professional development. The curriculum follows health and illness across the lifespan and includes projects in medical science, sustainable public health, technology and healthcare organisation.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options offer related scientific study of health and disease, with different emphases on biomedicine, health technology and population health. They do not provide the integrated clinical training in patient interviews, physical examination and treatment planning that forms part of Medicine. They do not qualify students to practise medicine or guarantee admission to a medical master.

curriculum.limitation: The Erasmus year groups show workload, not separate course awards: 30 EC is awarded at the first-year progression decision, 30 EC after the minor and the remaining credits at final assessment. Individual blocks and projects have no separate EC allocation.

componentNotes.y1-integrated: Five case-based medical blocks, two projects and integrated clinical, professional, societal, academic and technology teaching. The 60 EC represents workload across the first year.
componentNotes.y2-integrated: Homeostasis, regulation, reproduction and digestion, two projects and integrated longitudinal teaching. The 60 EC represents workload across the second year.
componentNotes.y3-minor: 30 EC of broadening minor study; combinations with approved electives are permitted under the programme rules.
componentNotes.y3-integrated: Final integrated medical blocks and competency-linked final works. The 29 EC is the remaining workload after the minor and separately counted professionalism requirement.
componentNotes.professionalism: 1 EC awarded for sufficient longitudinal professional conduct at the final examination; included in the 180-EC total.

concepts.label: Biomedical science, health & behaviour
concepts.concept: This biomedical programme studies normal body structure and function, cellular and biochemical processes, pathology, immunity, pharmacology, brain and behaviour, health psychology, epidemiology and research. Its substantial health-science content responds to the scientific foundations of Medicine. It does not reproduce Erasmus’s integrated clinical reasoning, patient interviewing, physical examination, supervised care or professional formation, and it does not qualify a student to practise medicine.

concepts.label: Health technology, data & AI
concepts.concept: A health-technology programme connects physiology, disease mechanisms, pathology, pharmacology, cognition and evidence synthesis with programming, mathematics, data management, machine learning, image analysis, deep learning, robotics and AI ethics. The computing courses provide methods for investigating health technologies; their projects are not assumed to use clinical datasets or devices. The biomedical base and AI ethics supply substantive health questions. This is scientific and technological study rather than training to deliver clinical care.

concepts.label: Population health, prevention & society
concepts.concept: A population-health programme combines epidemiology, infection, disease mechanisms, physiology and pharmacology with health psychology, lifespan development, statistics and evidence synthesis. Social psychology, sociology, ethics, public and behavioural economics, qualitative methods, organisational psychology and scientific communication support the study of prevention, unequal health and healthcare organisation. The policy and organisational courses supply general analytical tools; they are not specialist health-policy or clinical training.

components: Workload accounting group: five case-based blocks (healthy start; growth/development I and II; infection/immunity; internal/external threats), Medical Science and Sustainable Public Health projects, and all five integrated longitudinal lines. This is not a separately awarded 60-EC course.

Workload accounting group: Homeostasis I and II, Regulation, Reproduction/Gynaecology, Food Intake/Processing, Health & Technology and Care Policy & Organisation projects, and the five integrated longitudinal lines. This is not a separately awarded 60-EC course.
A 30-EC broadening minor completed in the first half of year 3 under the programme's minor rules.

Remaining workload accounting group after the 30-EC minor and separately specified 1-EC professionalism requirement: posture/movement, brain/senses, ageing/end of life, integrated lines and competency-linked final works. No individual block EC is inferred.
